title: A/R Summary: 30 customers at a time, none repeated or skipped
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: Between 31 and 90 customers owe you money, so A/R Summary loads them 30 at a time as you scroll.
  • You are an Admin user (the "Admin" role) working at {Location-A}, your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Between 31 and 90 customers have open documents on today's date.
    For example: the QA organization's A/R Summary has 46 customers.
  • Starting screen: A/R Summary (Reports, then "A/R Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  2. Open the CSV and count the customers in it (each name once).
  3. Count the customers shown before any more load (or compare them with the first 30 names in the CSV) and note the last one.
  4. Scroll down until the next customers load.
  5. Keep scrolling to the end of the list, writing down each customer's name.
  6. Click the "Total" header.
  7. Scroll from the top to the end of the list again, writing down each name.
  8. In the Past due filter, tick "1-30 days".
  9. Tick "91+ days".
  10. Scroll from the top to the end of the list again, writing down each name.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the CSV downloads.
  • Step 2: note the number of customers (for example 46).
  • Step 3: exactly 30 customers.
  • Step 4: the next customers load below as you scroll (there are no page buttons), starting with the customer that comes right after the last one noted in step 3, not a repeat.
  • Step 5: every customer appears exactly once and the count equals the CSV's.
  • Step 6: the rows sort by Total, largest first.
  • Step 7: in this sort too, every customer appears exactly once and none is missing.
  • Step 8: the chip reads "Past due: 1-30 days" and the report reloads with that range only.
  • Step 9: the chip reads "Past due: 2 ranges" and the report reloads with both ranges.
  • Step 10: every customer left by the filter appears exactly once; none repeats as more load.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 9 (23 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 26 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order)

  • S1-R8: “A/R Summary, A/P Summary, A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices show 30 customers or vendors at a time, and the next 30 load as the user scrolls down, as today. There are no page buttons. A/R Detail and A/P Detail show each bucket's first 100 lines, then load more as the user scrolls (S4-R4). Paging never repeats or skips a customer, vendor or row, in any sort.”
  • What changes for existing users: “A/R reports no longer come out in an unpredictable order; A/R Summary and A/R Collection no longer repeat or skip customers between pages.”
